clue.text: Literary gossip — the academic's curse

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk about a person, a literary gossip collection
taken as written
an MA, a Master of Arts, is an academic; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A bookish tittle-tattle is apparently what a scholar dreads most.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accursed or detested, a formal ecclesiastical ban, is exactly this word's meaning.

clue.text: Nearly everyone has an objection

parts.note: all means everyone
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Almost everybody has some complaint to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means almost, as in all but finished.

clue.text: Coming into office to get an increase

definitions.meaning: a monarch's or official's taking up of a post or throne
an addition, such as a new item added to a library

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of attaining or adding: a ruler's start and an addition.

clue.text: Offer rejected when below reserve

indicators.note: in a down answer, below puts the second piece under the first

parts.note: to hold is to keep in reserve
out means rejected, as a proposal is ruled out

explanation.surface: An auction bid turned down when it falls short of the reserve price.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out a hand or hope is to proffer it.

clue.text: Low points for Titania and Oberon, for example

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
N and S are compass points, north and south

explanation.surface: Low moments for the fairy king and queen of the play.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania and Oberon are Shakespeare's fairy rulers, but here they are satellites of Uranus.
explanation.definitionFit: Two of the planet Uranus's satellites carry these Shakespearean names.

clue.text: Behaves badly, in a state with drink

parts.note: ACT, the Australian Capital Territory, is a federal unit of Australia, loosely called a state
to sup is to drink, and a sup is a mouthful

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves when worked up and having had a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To play up or misbehave, as a child or a machine does, is the phrasal verb's sense.

clue.text: Trick questions in competition

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a test is a set of questions

explanation.surface: A quiz uses trick questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest is a competition between rivals.

clue.text: Checks removing unknowns from operating procedures

indicators.note: removing means the following letters are taken out of the word for operating procedures

parts.note: systems are methods or procedures for operating
Y is an algebraic unknown, so unknowns is YS

explanation.surface: Reviews that strip uncertainties out of standard procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing' takes YS from SYSTEMS, leaving STEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to check or stop it.

clue.text: Take options on low lands

parts.note: puts are options to sell, so taking options can mean buying puts
down means low or depressed

explanation.surface: Buying options on cheap, poor-quality land.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot who lands an aircraft is said to set it down.

clue.text: Surgeon starts to take action about conclusion of bitter dispute

indicators.note: about means going round, so the surgeon's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
an end is a conclusion

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A surgeon begins legal action to settle a feud.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud.

clue.text: Misguidedly gave men control, following Liberal sort of administration

indicators.note: following tells us the L comes first and the rest follows after it
misguidedly suggests the words gave men control are steered wrongly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a Liberal regime foolishly handed power to the men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like a political adjective qualifying the administration, but it only supplies its abbreviation; 'Misguidedly' is the anagram signal for the three words before the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Councils running towns and counties form a kind of administration below national level.

clue.text: Sunspot disturbance clears

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of sunspot are jumbled

explanation.surface: Solar activity is said to brighten the skies.
explanation.definitionFit: To unblock a drain or pipe is to clear it of an obstruction.

clue.text: Prepared to be turned out

definitions.meaning: food that is ... is made ready, as with a salad or a carcass
someone well turned out is smartly clothed

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both clothed and readied, as a dressed crab is prepared for the table.

clue.text: Break traditions? Not on-and not with it!

indicators.note: to break the word traditions is to rearrange it, after the letters of on are taken away as the clue says Not on

explanation.surface: Someone rebels against customs and ends up confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' takes ON out of TRADITIONS, leaving TRADITIS, and 'Break' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrait means absent-minded or distracted, as someone not paying attention would be.

clue.text: European gold put on special trains

indicators.note: in a down answer, put on places the gold on top of the next piece

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: special suggests an unusual arrangement, so the letters of trains are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller from the Continent uses golden special trains.
explanation.definitionFit: An Austrian is a native of a central European country.

clue.text: The detailed argument put one off one's stroke

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, the word losing its final letter

parts.note: a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: Getting into an involved quarrel disrupts a person's rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as de-tailed: THE loses its last letter to give TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert or confuse someone is to throw them, as in being thrown by a question.

clue.text: Reserve notes on judgment, say

indicators.note: in a down answer, on places the first piece above the next

parts.note: re and ti are notes of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: say signals that what follows is pronounced, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: sense is good judgment

explanation.surface: Keep notes on one's judgment, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as in restraint or reluctance to speak openly.

clue.text: Plausible but false promises to pay after commercial venture

indicators.note: after places the promises below the venture in a down answer

parts.note: a spec is a speculative business venture
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Dodgy promises of payment after a business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means seemingly right but actually wrong.

clue.text: Taught about appropriate sound of old language

annotationWithheld.why: Taught about appropriate sound of old language (5): PUNIC; NIC may be a sound-alike of NICK (appropriate), but no honest reading of 'Taught about' gives PU
annotationWithheld.clue: Taught about appropriate sound of old language

clue.text: Where to put the plate in a restaurant?

definitions.text: Where to put the plate in a restaurant?

parts.words: Where to put the plate in a restaurant?
parts.note: plate means cutlery or silverware, kept in a fitted box, while the same word also names a works dining room

explanation.surface: A diner wonders where to set the dish down.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is both a works restaurant and a case of cutlery.

clue.text: Want to have lasting effect on financial centre

parts.note: a scar is a lasting mark left by an injury or trauma
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A wish to make a lasting mark on the world of finance.
explanation.walkthrough: THE CITY is the City of London, Britain's banking and finance district.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or shortage: a dearth of something.

clue.text: Priest accepts suitable collar

indicators.note: accepts means taking something inside, so the priest's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
apt means suitable

explanation.surface: A clergyman puts on an appropriate dog collar.
explanation.definitionFit: To collar a suspect is to catch or seize them.

clue.text: Poor nun beginning to take a drink

parts.note: a Poor Clare is a nun of the order of St Clare

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An impoverished sister starts drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Daily newspaper's leaders not in code

annotationWithheld.why: Daily newspaper's leaders not in code (7): CLEANER; NE inside CLEAR needs 'in' both inside the phrase 'not in code' (CLEAR) and as the insertion indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Daily newspaper's leaders not in code

clue.text: First appearance for actor required to take the lead

definitions.meaning: the moment a player comes on stage
in bridge, a card able to win a trick and so give the lead to a hand

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean a way in: coming on stage and gaining access to a hand at cards.

clue.text: Local question put to a Labour leader

parts.note: a question under discussion is a topic

indicators.note: a leader is the front letter of the word Labour that follows

explanation.surface: A constituent's question addressed to a party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a topical treatment is applied to one area only, so it is local.

clue.text: Volunteers know what's needed

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve
ken means know, in Scots

explanation.surface: Volunteers understand what is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Time taken is the time required, so it means needed.

clue.text: Supine monarch, after blaze, receiving little attention

indicators.note: after puts the monarch's letters behind those for blaze

parts.note: supine means lying face upward, flat on the back
to blaze is to burn
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch

explanation.surface: A ruler lying flat after a fire is neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on a stove's rear ring is left simmering, so the idiom means postponed or neglected.

clue.text: Saw part of essay ingeniously written

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters run inside the words essay ingeniously

explanation.surface: A remark on a cleverly written piece of an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim.

clue.text: New name, either outlandish or native

indicators.note: outlandish means bizarre, so the letters are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: A new name may seem foreign or homegrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Native in the sense of innate or intrinsic, a quality belonging by nature.
